_meta.scope: Commercial gym chains in London. Council leisure centres and boutique studios are a separate agent's file.
_meta.rule: Every figure below was read off the operator's own website on 9 September 2026. No comparison site, affiliate roundup or news article was used.
_meta.priceIsPerClub: Gym pricing in London is set per club, not per brand. Every range below names the specific London clubs the cheapest and dearest figures come from. Where a brand publishes one London-wide price, that is said explicitly.
_meta.promoWarning: Several chains are running joining-fee promotions today. Where a fee is £0 because of an offer rather than as standing policy, that is stated in the joiningFee field.
unconfirmed: Anytime Fitness — anytimefitness.co.uk redirects to anytimefitness.com/en-gb, which served an Imperva bot-protection interstitial ("Additional security check is required") with a CAPTCHA on every attempt today, in a real browser as well as by script. No London club list, price or joining fee could be taken from the operator's own site. Ask Rob.

Snap Fitness monthly prices — club pages carry day-pass prices and terms but route monthly membership to a "Submit Interest" form rather than publishing a figure. The £30 standing joining fee is confirmed from the operator's own promo wording.

énergie Fitness monthly prices — the memberships block on every London club page is loaded by script and returns no price in the served HTML. The no-joining-fee offers ARE in the served HTML and are recorded.
Bannatyne joining fee amount — the site advertises "50% off the joining fee" but the underlying amount is only revealed inside the joinus.bannatyne.co.uk flow, which is script-driven.

Gymbox Westfield Shepherds Bush — listed as one of the 10 clubs but /gyms/shepherds-bush/ and /memberships/shepherds-bush/ both return a stub page with no membership panel.
Virgin Active prices for 27 of its 32 London clubs — see the Virgin Active entry. This is the operator's choice, not a scraping failure.

brands.cheapestClub: London Croydon and London Wembley, both £22.99 Core
brands.joiningFee: Charged, and set per club: £0 to £25. Today 5 of 87 London clubs charge £0 (Camden High Street, Chiswick Park, Cricklewood, Harrow, Kensington High Street) — that is the SAVEHALF promotion, not the standing price. The commonest London fee is £15 (25 clubs), then £20 (18), then £19.99 (14). The dearest London fees are £25 at Bow Wharf, Fulham, Limehouse, Moorgate, Piccadilly and St Pauls, and £24.99 at Aldgate, Clapham, East Sheen, Holborn and Hoxton. PureGym's own terms: "Joining fees are applied to cover the initial administration costs associated with setting up a new membership and direct debit agreement and entitle the member to an induction session, bookable online." A site-wide banner today reads "get 50% off your first month and £0 joining fee. Use code: SAVEHALF. Hurry, ends midnight! Selected gyms only".
brands.contract: Rolling, no contract, on all three monthly tiers. A fixed-term option (6, 9 or 12 months paid in advance) saves up to 10%.
brands.pool: No. No PureGym in London has a swimming pool, and PureGym does not claim one anywhere on its gym pages.
brands.offPeak: Yes, at 61 of 87 London clubs — so a quarter of London PureGyms have no off-peak tier at all. London off-peak prices run £17.99 (Croydon, Wembley) to £35.99 (Clapham, Fulham). PureGym's own footnote: "Off peak hours vary by gym, please check join process for details." The hours are not published on the gym pages.
brands.multiSite: Only on the Plus tier, and it is capped: "Get access to every other full priced PureGym at the same price or lower than yours." Join a cheap outer-London club on Plus and central London is not included. London Plus prices run £28.99 (Croydon) to £59.99 (Clapham).
brands.freeze: Off-Peak and Core: from £6.99 for up to 3 months. Plus: free for up to 3 months in a 12-month period.
brands.cancellation: Monthly memberships cancel any time. Fixed-term is the trap: "You can cancel you fixed-term membership anytime. Get a refund of 50% of the remaining credit on the account from the day you contact us." Half the unused balance is kept.
brands.buriedTerm: The Plus multi-gym tier only opens gyms priced at or below your home gym. Buy Plus at Croydon (£28.99) and you cannot use Clapham (£59.99). Buy it at Clapham and you can use everything. The tier that sounds like a nationwide pass is really a price band.
brands.dayPass: Sold, 1 to 30 days, "no contract or sign up fees". Price set per gym.
brands.guest: Not included on Core or Off-Peak. Plus brings a guest 4 times a month at no extra cost. Everyone else can add the Buddy Access bolt-on "from just £3 extra per month" for 4 guest visits a month.
brands.hours247: Not universal. 68 of 87 open London club pages are titled "24 hour gym"; PureGym's own footnote is "†Most gyms open 24/7". London Holborn is 24/7; several are not.
brands.classes: Included at most gyms. Core books 8 days ahead, Plus 14 days.
brands.londonPriceSpread: Off-peak £17.99–£35.99, Core £22.99–£49.99, Plus £28.99–£59.99. The dearest London club (Clapham) costs 2.2x the cheapest (Croydon) for the identical Core product.
brands.notes: Two more London sites are not yet open: New Malden (Opening Soon) and Sidcup (Coming Soon). Excluded from all figures above.
brands.source: https://www.puregym.com/gyms/ (all 89 London club pages read individually), https://www.puregym.com/membership-options/, https://www.puregym.com/membership-terms-conditions/, https://www.puregym.com/membership-options/bolt-ons/buddy-access/

brands.cheapestClub: London Alperton, London Colindale and London Wembley Central, all £23.99 Standard
brands.joiningFee: Charged, and set per club: £0, £10, £15 or £20 depending on the club. Today 45 of 86 London clubs charge £15, 17 charge £10, 23 charge £0 and two charge £20 (London Staples Corner and London Surbiton). The Gym Group's own London region page still says "pay from £30.99 today including a one-off £10 joining fee" — that £10 is not what most London clubs actually charge. Its footer hedges: "Applicable terms, conditions and joining fees may apply." Saver plans (9 or 12 months paid up front) carry no joining fee at all.
brands.contract: Both. Pay Monthly is rolling with no commitment but "Joining fees apply". Saver plans are 9 or 12 months, paid up front or in 3 instalments, with no joining fee. At Oxford Street the gap is £37.99/month rolling Standard against £409 for 12 months (£34.08/month equivalent).
brands.pool: No. No Gym Group site in London has a swimming pool.
brands.offPeak: Yes at 79 of 86 London clubs, £16.99 (Croydon Purley Way, Feltham) to £32.99 (Monument). The hours are genuinely awkward and differ club to club — 11 distinct off-peak schedules across the London estate. A typical one runs 06:00–16:30 and 20:00–22:00 weekdays; another splits the day into 00:00–06:00, 09:00–11:00 and 13:00–16:30. Check the specific club.
brands.multiSite: Ultimate tier only. Standard and Off-Peak are single-gym. London Ultimate runs £29.99 (East Croydon) to £48.99 (Charing Cross, Monument).
brands.freeze: Ultimate only — "Freeze your monthly membership once for free". Standard and Off-Peak cannot freeze.
brands.cancellation: Pay Monthly cancels any time. Saver plans must run the full committed term before cancelling.
brands.buriedTerm: "Open 24/7" is the brand's headline and four London clubs are not. The Gym Group's own London FAQ names them: Caledonian Road (Mon–Fri 06:30–23:00, Sat–Sun 08:00–21:00), Charing Cross (Mon–Fri 6am–10pm, Sat–Sun 10am–5pm), East Ham High Street (Mon–Fri 6am–10pm, Sat–Sun 8am–8pm) and Oxford Street (Mon–Fri 6am–10pm, Sat–Sun 8am–8pm). Charing Cross and Oxford Street are two of the three dearest clubs in London.
brands.dayPass: Yes. 1 day £9.99–£16.99 depending on club (£9.99 at Alperton, Colindale, East Croydon; £16.99 at Monument). 3-day and 5-day passes also sold — £26.99 and £33.99 at Oxford Street.
brands.guest: Ultimate only ("Guest Passes"). Not available on Standard or Off-Peak.
brands.hours247: Most London clubs, but see buriedTerm for the four exceptions.
brands.classes: Free and included on all tiers. Personal training is not: "personal training is not included in your membership, and each Personal trainer is freelance and sets their rate." New members get one free PT session within 60 days of joining.
brands.londonPriceSpread: Off-peak £16.99–£32.99, Standard £23.99–£39.99, Ultimate £29.99–£48.99. Standard 12-month saver £259 (Colindale, East Croydon) to £449 (Monument).
brands.extraCosts: Lockers need your own padlock, or £5.00 from the vending machine.
brands.notes: Three more London sites are Opening Soon: Old Street, Putney, Richmond. Excluded. Watford, Dartford and Sunbury are listed under London on the site but are outside Greater London and excluded from the ranges (Watford £26.99, Dartford £27.99, Sunbury £25.99 Standard).

brands.joiningFee: None, and it is standing policy rather than an offer — "No Joining Fee" appears as a permanent feature bullet on every membership card at every club, including day passes and student rates. The only London chain of any size where this is unambiguously true.
brands.contract: Both. Standard and Plus+ are no-contract rolling. Annual is paid up front and gives 14 months for the price of 12 — £311 at Uxbridge (£22.21/month equivalent), £359 at Charlton (£25.64), £419 at Enfield (£29.93). Free freeze is not included on the Annual Saver.
brands.pool: No. None of the three London JD Gyms has a pool. Charlton and the others do have saunas in the changing rooms, included in the membership price.
brands.offPeak: No off-peak tier. JD Gyms sells one anytime price per club plus a multi-site upgrade.
brands.multiSite: Plus+ tier, £4–£5 a month more than Standard (£29.99 Uxbridge, £34.99 Charlton, £39.99 Enfield). The JD Gyms Plus+ page says "Train at 100+ JD Gyms across the UK", but the Uxbridge club page advertises Plus+ as "Use 55+ Gyms" while Charlton and Enfield say "Use 100+ Gyms". Worth checking what your specific club opens.
brands.freeze: Included on monthly memberships; expressly excluded from the Annual Saver — "Free freeze benefit is not included in the Annual Saver membership".
brands.cancellation: No contract on Standard and Plus+, cancel any time.
brands.buriedTerm: The first-month teaser rate is not the price. Enfield and Uxbridge both advertise "£15 1st month", then £34.99 and £25.99 respectively. Charlton has no teaser and charges £29.99 from month one — so the club that looks dearest on the shelf price is the cheapest of the three over a year.
brands.dayPass: £10.99 at Uxbridge, £11.99 at Charlton and Enfield. One-time entry by QR code in the JD Gyms app, valid 24 hours from purchase, full access to all facilities.
brands.guest: Not offered as a membership benefit; a guest buys a day pass.
brands.hours247: Yes, all three London clubs are open 24/7.
brands.classes: Included in every membership including the day pass.
brands.notes: Only three JD Gyms are in Greater London: London Charlton (Stone Lake Retail Park, Woolwich Rd, SE7 8LU), Enfield and Uxbridge. Watford, Harlow and Luton are outside London. Student rate is £9.99 for the first month, then the club's standard price.

brands.dearestClub: London Baker Street, London Bridge Cottons and London Marylebone, all £120 standard
brands.joiningFee: Charged, amount not published. The terms confirm it exists: "For new members who are paying via Direct Debit, your first payment including any joining fee will be paid upfront by card payment." No figure appears anywhere on the public site — the only London chain in this file that charges a joining fee without saying how much.
brands.contract: Minimum-term contracts with a monthly flexible alternative. The terms describe a fixed initial minimum term, and the settlement clause implies a standard 12-month option running roughly £15/month below the 1-month flexible rate.
brands.pool: Some sites, and here is the list. WITH a pool: Baker Street (17m, with private swimming tuition), Bishopsgate (16m), London Bridge Cottons (2m depth), Hammersmith (2m depth), Highbury (full-length), Streatham (20m), Thomas More Square Wapping (12m). WITHOUT: Balham, Brixton, Clapham Junction, Oxford Circus, Queens Park, The Strand. Fenchurch Street and Queen Victoria Street reference a pool only via their neighbour Thomas More Square, so treat those two as unconfirmed. Marylebone has none of its own — its page instead offers "access to our nearby Baker Street club, less than a mile away, where you can enjoy additional training facilities including swimming pool and sauna", and charges the same £120 as Baker Street for it.
brands.offPeak: No off-peak tier. Two prices are shown per club: Standard and Student (Baker Street £120/£99, Streatham £65/£49, Brixton £54/£45).
brands.multiSite: Included on every membership, but tiered: "Multi club access is determined by your club, meaning you can use any club at your membership tier or below. This excludes any single club memberships who have access to the club they join only." The club pages state the reach inconsistently — Bishopsgate and Queen Victoria Street say "22 other Fitness First gyms nationwide", Streatham says "13 other Fitness First gyms", and Baker Street lists only three named neighbours (Marylebone, Oxford Circus, The Strand).
brands.freeze: £8 a month, 1 to 3 months, only after your second month of membership, requested at least 5 working days before your direct debit date. Medical, relocation or other accepted reasons may qualify for a free freeze.
brands.cancellation: There is a cancellation charge. Seven days to change your mind, unless you have visited three or more times, in which case no refund. Leaving before the end of the minimum term means either paying the remaining balance or paying a settlement fee: "The settlement fee is the total discount and rate reduction you received through the contract length originally chosen, when compared to the 1-month flexible rate." Fitness First's own worked example: cancel after 3 months of a 12-month term, where the difference between the 1-month and 12-month price is £15 a month, and you pay £15 x 3 = £45. Free exit only for medical reasons, job loss, or moving more than five miles from your home club.
brands.buriedTerm: Clause 9 of the membership terms, and nothing else in London comes close: "If you use another club other than your home club more frequently over a two-month period, we may transfer your membership to that club, which could impact your fees." Join cheap at Brixton (£54), get a job near Baker Street (£120), use it more often for two months, and Fitness First reserves the right to move you onto the dearer club's rate. Second: clause 25 — a minimum-term membership auto-renews "into a new contract with the same minimum term" unless you give a calendar month's notice to end at the term date (clause 26 then allows cancel-any-time on the renewed contract as a "loyalty discount", so the renewal term is not in practice binding — but the two clauses sit one after the other and read in opposite directions). Third: "If you pay by monthly Direct Debit an additional charge for credit will be included in the membership fee" — paying monthly costs more than the sticker price.
brands.dayPass: Paid day passes are sold; terms are in the membership T&Cs. Price not published on club pages.
brands.extraCosts: Reformer Pilates runs on a credit system at clubs where it is not included — individual credits are £10 each via the app, valid 60 days, non-refundable, and forfeited credits from late cancellation are not reinstated. Locker hire needs a £30 refundable deposit, forfeited if you lose the key. Class no-shows: cancel less than 24 hours before and "repeated non-attendance of booked classes may result in members class booking access being revoked".
brands.classes: Included, roughly 2,000 a week nationally, bookable in advance.
brands.londonClubs: Baker Street, Balham, Bishopsgate, London Bridge Cottons, Brixton, Clapham Junction, Fenchurch Street, Hammersmith, Highbury, Liverpool Street, Marylebone, Oxford Circus, Queen Victoria Street, Queens Park, Streatham, The Strand, Thomas More Square Wapping. That is 17 of the 25 Fitness First clubs in the UK.

brands.dearestClub: Barbican, City and Moorgate, all £137 Anytime on a 12-month commitment
brands.joiningFee: £29 one-time at every London club except three City sites at £39 (Barbican, City, Moorgate — Moorgate charges £29 on off-peak and £39 on the two anytime plans, which is the only inconsistency in the estate). Nuffield publishes it plainly on every plan card: "£29.00 one-time joining fee". It is not framed as a promotion and there is no offer waiving it — the most honest joining-fee disclosure of any chain in this file.
brands.contract: Both, and the gap is published per club. Off-peak and Anytime are both 12-month commitments; 1-month rolling has no commitment. At Covent Garden: off-peak £77, Anytime £90 on 12 months, rolling £107. The rolling premium runs £17–£25 a month across London — roughly 18–20% for the right to leave.
brands.pool: Yes at 31 of 33 London clubs. NO pool at exactly two: Battersea (facilities are a cycling studio, squash courts, sauna and steam room) and Bromley (NuCycle studio, Nu Kitchen and Technogym kit — no pool and no sauna listed). This matters because Nuffield's membership panel prints the same boilerplate on every club page including those two: "All plans include full access to the gym floor, swimming pool, sauna and steam room, plus unlimited fitness classes." At Battersea and Bromley that sentence is simply not true of the club you would be joining. Two more clubs list a pool only in the welcome copy and not in the amenity tiles — Brondesbury Park, Moorgate and Twickenham all confirm a pool elsewhere on the page, so read the welcome bullets rather than the tiles.
brands.offPeak: Yes at 32 of 33 London clubs (the City club sells Anytime and rolling only), and the hours vary wildly from club to club — this is the thing to check. Eight distinct London off-peak schedules: Covent Garden and Battersea are 09:00–17:00 weekdays with weekends free; Twickenham is 06:30–16:00 weekdays with weekends free; Bromley is 06:00–16:00 weekdays with no weekend access at all; one club runs 09:30–15:30 weekdays and only 15:30–21:00 at weekends; another splits the weekday into 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00. London off-peak prices run £65 (Battersea, Ilford) to £116 (Barbican, Moorgate).
brands.multiSite: "Multi-club access" is listed as a benefit on every London club page. Nuffield does not publish the tier rules on the club pages.
brands.freeze: Not published on the club pages.
brands.cancellation: 12-month commitment on off-peak and Anytime; 1-month rolling is "cancel anytime".
brands.buriedTerm: The 12-month Anytime plan is sold as "Save with a longer term commitment" and the rolling plan as "Maximum flexibility" — but the discount for tying yourself in for a year is only about £17–£25 a month, and the off-peak plan, which is also a 12-month commitment, is where the real saving sits. At Islington the ladder is £109 off-peak, £128 Anytime, £150 rolling: the off-peak tier saves £41 a month, more than twice what the contract saves. And what off-peak buys differs so much by club that the same £109 might be 09:00–17:00 weekdays plus all weekend, or weekdays only with no weekend access.
brands.dayPass: Complimentary 3-day gym pass offered at club level; a paid day-pass page exists.
brands.promoActive: Battersea is running 20% off today — Anytime £61 (was £76) and rolling £74 (was £93). It is the only London club showing a discounted rate; every other price in this file is the standing price.
brands.londonPriceSpread: Off-peak £65–£116. Anytime 12-month £77–£137. Rolling £97–£159. The City trio (Barbican, City, Moorgate) at £137/£159 costs 78% more than Ilford at £77/£97 for the same product with the same joining structure.

brands.cheapestClub: Canary Riverside and Strand, both £160 a month on 12 months (£218 rolling)
brands.dearestClub: Chiswick Riverside, £300 a month on 12 months (£404 rolling)
brands.joiningFee: Charged at every club, set per club, and the spread is enormous — from £25 to £250. Virgin Active states it on the club's own rates page: Strand "A £25 joining fee applies to all 12 month memberships. A £50 joining fee applies to all monthly memberships." Canary Riverside £30 / £50. Kensington "A £45 joining fee applies to all 12 month memberships. A £75 joining fee applies to monthly memberships." Mayfair and Chiswick Riverside "A £250 joining fee applies to all membership types." So the joining fee is ten times higher at Mayfair than at Strand, and at most clubs it is doubled if you choose the rolling plan over the 12-month one. This is the largest joining fee of any London gym chain in this file.
brands.contract: Both. The rolling premium is severe: Mayfair £250 on 12 months against £315 rolling (+26%); Kensington £200 against £259.99 (+30%); Strand and Canary Riverside £160 against £218 (+36%); Chiswick Riverside £300 against £404 (+35%). Add the doubled joining fee on rolling and the flexibility costs real money.
brands.pool: Yes at almost every London club, and Virgin Active publishes the length on each club's overview page. Aldersgate 20m plus a hydrotherapy pool; Bank 16m; Bromley 25m; Canary Riverside 20m; Chiswick Park 25m; Clapham 17m plus hydrotherapy; Crouch End 16m; Islington Angel 25m; Mayfair 20m; Mill Hill 20m; Moorgate 25m; Notting Hill 20m; Repton Park 24m; Streatham 14m; Swiss Cottage 25m; Wandsworth Smugglers Way 25m; Wimbledon Worple Road 20m; Chiswick Riverside has pools plus tennis and padel; Fulham Pools is built around the Fulham Council Pool. No pool is described on the Barbican, Chelsea, Cricklewood, Hammersmith, Mansion House, Merchant Square, Tower Bridge, Twickenham or Walbrook (Cannon Street) overview pages — those pages served a generic shell today and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than pool-free.
brands.offPeak: No off-peak tier is published. The published age tiers are the discount instead: 16–17 rolling monthly, 18–25 on 12 months and 65+ on 12 months all pay 15% less than the standard 12-month rate (Mayfair £212.50, Kensington £170, Strand £136).
brands.multiSite: Tiered, seven tiers, and Virgin Active publishes the full table (last edited 21 August 2026): "You can visit any club in your membership tier or below. Tier 1 is the highest tier and Tier 7 is the lowest." Tier 1: Chiswick Riverside and Mayfair (both badged [Collection]). Tier 2: Kensington. Tier 3: Aldersgate, Bank, Canary Riverside, Cannon Street, Chiswick Park, Clapham, Crouch End, Strand, Wimbledon. Tier 4: Bromley, Clearview, Fulham Pools, Islington Angel, Mill Hill, Moorgate, Northampton Collingtree Park, Notting Hill, Repton Park, Swiss Cottage, Wandsworth. Tier 5: Chelmsford, Northampton Riverside Park, Nottingham, Sheffield Broadfield Park, Solihull, Thundersley. Tier 6: Salford Quays, Streatham. The tiers line up exactly with the published prices, which is how you can infer roughly what an unpriced club costs.
brands.cancellation: not published on the rates pages.
brands.buriedTerm: Virgin Active publishes a price for only 5 of its 32 London clubs. Mayfair, Chiswick Riverside, Kensington, Canary Riverside and Strand have a MEMBERSHIP RATES page with figures on it. The other 27 — Aldersgate, Bank, Barbican, Broadgate, Bromley, Chelsea, Chiswick Park, Clapham, Cricklewood, Crouch End, Fulham Pools, Hammersmith, Islington Angel, Mansion House, Merchant Square, Mill Hill, Moorgate, Notting Hill, Repton Park, Swiss Cottage, Tower Bridge, Twickenham, Walbrook, Wandsworth Smugglers Way, Wimbledon Worple Road and the rest — have a memberships page that shows no price at all, only links to multi-club access, corporate, family and Vitality. You have to book a tour to find out what it costs.

brands.joiningFee: not published.
brands.contract: Two lengths, both published: "Standard — Initial 12 calendar month term" and "Flexible — Initial 3 calendar month term". Even the flexible option has a three-month minimum, and it is not available everywhere: "3 month membership is not available at David Lloyd Bury St Edmunds, Colliers Wood, Edinburgh Shawfair, Harlow, Herne Bay, Notting Hill and Rugby." Two of those seven — Colliers Wood and Notting Hill — are London clubs, so at those two the only option is twelve months.
brands.pool: Yes, at every London club, and it is the point of the brand. Kensington is titled "Gym with indoor swimming pool in Kensington" and has two gyms, a heated indoor pool, saunas, steam room and hydropool. Membership tiers Platinum, Club Plus and Club all include Swimming Pool. Indoor and outdoor pools across the estate.
brands.offPeak: Yes — the entry tier is an off-peak tier and David Lloyd publishes the hours: "Club — Gives you access to our facilities at off-peak times during the day: 11am-4pm weekdays and after 2pm weekends. You'll miss out on access to racquets, exclusive spa facilities and Blaze classes." An 11am–4pm weekday window is the narrowest off-peak of any chain in this file.
brands.multiSite: Platinum only — "access to all facilities at your home Club, plus access to selected other Clubs and facilities" and "Access to luxury Spa Retreats". Club Plus and Club are home-club only.
brands.cancellation: not published beyond the minimum terms.
brands.buriedTerm: David Lloyd publishes no price anywhere. Its memberships page is an enquiry funnel — choose a club, a duration, a tier and a membership type, then "Enquire now" — with the disclaimer "Not all packages are available at all Clubs and facilities do vary by Club, but our team will help find the best package for you based on your preferences." That means the price is negotiated, which in turn means the price you are quoted depends on how you negotiate. Second buried term: the Platinum guest pass, one of the main reasons to pay for the top tier, is withdrawn at five London clubs — "Monthly guest pass on a Platinum membership unavailable at Acton Park, Bushey, Derby, Enfield, Finchley, Hampton, Hull, Leeds, Lincoln, Newcastle, Northwood, Nottingham West Bridgford and Teesside." Acton Park, Enfield, Finchley, Hampton and Northwood are all London.
brands.tiers: Platinum (gym, pool, classes, racquets, Blaze, unrestricted hours, monthly guest pass, fresh towel every visit, 10% off bar and restaurant, multi-club, spa retreats); Club Plus (gym, pool, classes, unrestricted hours — no racquets, no Blaze, no spa, no guest pass); Club (gym, pool, classes, off-peak 11am–4pm weekdays and after 2pm weekends only).

brands.dearestClub: Farringdon and Victoria, £141 a month on a rolling monthly contract (£108 on 12 months)
brands.joiningFee: Charged, and it changes with the contract length rather than the club: £30 on the rolling monthly plan, £10 on the 3-month plan, and £10 or £0 on the 12-month plan depending on the club. Bank and Holborn charge £10 on 12 months; Ealing, Elephant and Castle, Farringdon, Finsbury Park, Victoria and Westfield Stratford show £0. Gymbox is explicit that the £0 is promotional — "£0 joining fee, down from £30" — so £30 is the standing fee and everything below it is an offer.
brands.contract: Three lengths, all published per club: 12 months, 3 months, and rolling monthly. Bank £95 / £120 / £130. Holborn and Old Street £82 / £102 / £112. Finsbury Park £105 / £128 / £138. Westfield Stratford £97 / £119 / £129. Ealing and Elephant and Castle £103 / £128 / £138. Farringdon and Victoria £108 / £131 / £141. The rolling premium is £30–£35 a month, about 35%.
brands.pool: No. No Gymbox has a pool. Saunas at every club, plus red light therapy, snow shower and hyperbaric oxygen therapy at Farringdon.
brands.offPeak: No off-peak tier.
brands.multiSite: Two prices per club — the figures above are single-gym. "Upgrade to all-gyms access to train across all 10 Gymbox clubs for a bit more per month." The all-gyms figure is not stated as a number on the club pages; at Westfield Stratford the second pair of figures on the page is £119/£129 against the single-gym £117/£127, suggesting roughly £2 a month, but the label is not published.
brands.cancellation: "On a monthly rolling plan, you can cancel at any time with one full calendar month's notice. On a 3-month or 12-month plan, the commitment period must be completed before you can cancel. After the initial term, all plans continue on a rolling monthly basis until cancelled."
brands.buriedTerm: The 50%-off offer on the 12-month plan has a named expiry that is not the end of your discount but the start of full price: "Get 50% off your first six months when you join. Your membership will then automatically go to the full price in April 2027." So a Farringdon sign-up sees £54 a month on the card, pays that for six months, and then pays £108 for the remaining six months of a contract they cannot leave. The advertised price is half the price you will actually average.
brands.dayPass: Free trial at every club, no payment details required.
brands.guest: 5 free guest passes a year on every plan, at every club.
brands.classes: Unlimited, included, across 7 categories (Aerial, Fight, Ride, Strength, Holistic, Rhythm, Sweat). 100+ a week at Farringdon, 75+ at Bank. Resident DJs.
brands.londonClubs: Bank, Ealing, Elephant and Castle, Farringdon, Finsbury Park, Holborn, Old Street, Victoria, Westfield Shepherds Bush, Westfield Stratford. All ten are in London — Gymbox is a London-only chain.
brands.notes: Westfield Shepherds Bush is listed as one of the 10 clubs but its /gyms/ and /memberships/ pages both return a stub with no membership panel, so no price for it.
brands.source: https://gymbox.com/memberships/ and all 10 club pages read individually

brands.cheapestClub: Canary Wharf, City, Moorgate and Wood Wharf, all £257 a month for single-club access
brands.dearestClub: Mayfair and Chelsea publish no single-club price at all — the only way into either is Group Plus at £345 a month. Of the clubs that do publish one, Islington, Marylebone, Soho and The Whiteley are dearest at £287.
brands.joiningFee: £100 on the Club and Group tiers, £200 on Group Plus. Third Space states it on every club page: "Memberships will be subject to a £100 joining fee" / "£200 joining fee". Not framed as promotional and no offer waiving it.
brands.contract: not published on the club pages.
brands.pool: Yes at most clubs, and Third Space publishes the size. Named on the club pages: Canary Wharf 20m, Islington 20m with 6 lanes, Marylebone 16m with 3 lanes, Soho 20m, The Whiteley a 3-lane Italian porcelain pool, Wimbledon 25m with 4 lanes, Wood Wharf 20m. Canary Wharf also has a cold plunge pool. The remaining club pages did not render a facilities list today, so treat Battersea, Chelsea, City, Clapham Junction, Mayfair, Moorgate, Paternoster Square, Queen's Park, Richmond and Tower Bridge as unconfirmed rather than pool-free.
brands.offPeak: No off-peak tier.
brands.multiSite: Three tiers and the middle one has a hole in it. Club (£257–£287) is single-club. Group (£299) "includes full access to all Third Space clubs, excluding Mayfair and Chelsea". Group Plus (£345) "includes use of all Third Space Clubs". So the two clubs most people picture when they think of Third Space are the two the £299 tier does not open.
brands.freeze: "Yes, simply give us 7 days' notice and pay a £40 monthly fee. You can freeze your membership for up to 6 months each year in 1-month increments." £40 a month to not use the gym is the highest freeze charge in this file — Fitness First charges £8, PureGym £6.99, The Gym Group nothing on its top tier.
brands.cancellation: not published on the club pages.
brands.buriedTerm: You pay for a club you may not be able to use yet. Every membership tier on every club page carries the same warning: "Initial access to these clubs will be staggered due to waitlists and access dates to each club will be confirmed on joining." On the single-club tier: "Initial access to this club will be staggered due to waitlists, and your confirmed access date will be provided upon joining." You sign up, pay the £100 joining fee, and are then told when you can start.
brands.extraCosts: Private lockers £40 a month; Executive lockers £80 a month (adds laundry for 4 items a visit, 1 guest pass, and a monthly shake worth £8.95). Personal training "from £85 p/hour".

brands.buriedTerm: It is a class chain wearing a gym's clothes. 1Rebel describes itself as "13 London gyms" and its app is called "1Rebel king of gyms", but everything it sells is a booked class — RIDE, RUMBLE, RESHAPE, REFORMER, RADIATE and RESET. brands.answerToRobsQuestion: It is a chain rather than a single studio — 13 locations across London, from Liverpool Street in the east to High Street Kensington in the west — but it is a boutique class operator, not a gym chain. If the other agent is covering boutique studios, 1Rebel belongs in their file rather than this one. Recorded here so it is not lost between the two.
